subject: Temporary rate increase & one-time credit for launch traffic
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily@aurora-health.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary rate increase for product launch

Hi Hannah,

Quick one — we’re rolling our new patient triage feature next week (internal go-live 2026-02-19) and expect an initial traffic spike for ~72 hours as customers run baseline workloads. Our current Dedicated capacity is ~10M tokens/day; we expect a peak near 28–32M tokens/day for the launch window.

Can Redwood temporarily lift our per-second rate limit / quota for that window and what would the incremental cost look like? We’re also curious whether you can provide a small one-time credit given this is a short-term, high-impact launch.

Attached is our usage snapshot from the past 30 days to help estimate (aurora_usage_report_feb.csv).

Thanks — Emily
Emily Zhao
Director of Product
Aurora Health

[Attachment: aurora_usage_report_feb.csv (csv)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@aurora-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate increase for product launch

Hi Emily — thanks for the heads up and the usage file, that helps.

Short answer: yes — we can provision a short-term rate/quot a bump and offer two practical paths:

1) Emergency burst window (recommended for <7 days)
   - Provisioned short window with a soft cap increase to 35M tokens/day and a sustained p95 per-second rate bump.
   - One-time management fee + usage billed at overage rate.
   - Optionally apply a one-time launch credit (see proposal below).

2) Temporary reserved uplift (recommended if you want predictable invoice)
   - Create a temporary higher reserved commit for 30 days at a discounted uplift rate.
   - More predictable billing but requires PO/invoice path.

Ballpark numbers (subject to finance sign-off):
- Overage billing: $0.008 per 1k tokens over committed quota for the burst window.
- One-time launch credit we can consider: $3,500 applied to the next invoice if Aurora signs the temporary uplift SOW.

I’ve looped in Ben (SE) to confirm technical feasibility for the exact window and Laura (finance) will need to confirm invoicing/credit approval if you want the SOW path. I’ll put together a short SOW draft and estimated invoice — do you prefer DocuSign or a straight PO + invoice?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Inline: proposed next steps]
- Confirm exact start/end times for the burst window (we recommend UTC 2026-02-19 00:00 — 2026-02-22 00:00).
- If you want a guaranteed uplift, sign SOW (attached draft will follow).

[Attachment: RDW_temp_burst_SOW_draft.pdf (pdf) — sent in follow-up]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate increase for product launch

Hannah / Marissa — technical note for the record:

- We can safely increase both per-second rate and daily quota for the requested 72h window. The runtime supports an automatic fallback to smaller model variants if we see sustained queuing beyond the burst profile.
- For a 35M/day cap, we recommend enabling prefix-KV caching and setting a 250ms token budget per request for best latency behavior under load.
- There is a small risk (~5%) of transient 503s at extreme burst corners if upstream spikes concentrate in short bursts; we can mitigate with a staged ramp (10%/30%/60% over first 6 hours).

I’ve sketched the ramp schedule and latency trade-offs in the attached SOW draft. If they want guaranteed SLOs we’ll need an elevated SLA addendum (legal).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@aurora-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate increase for product launch

Emily — attaching the draft SOW and a proposed invoice terms PDF. Summary of the offer:

- 72-hour burst window: 2026-02-19 00:00 UTC to 2026-02-22 00:00 UTC.
- Temporary quota increase to 35M tokens/day, p95 per-second uplift to match expected concurrency.
- Overage rate during the window: $0.008 / 1k tokens beyond committed quota.
- One-time launch credit: $3,500 applied if SOW signed within 48 hours.
- Ramp plan: staged 10%/30%/60% over first 6 hours to reduce transient errors.
- Billing: apply credit on next monthly invoice; if Aurora prefers immediate net-credit we can route via PO and credit memo (finance needs 3 business days).

Please confirm whether Aurora will:
- Sign the SOW (DocuSign link will be provided), and
- Confirm the exact UTC start time for the window.

If you prefer the temporary reserved uplift instead of overage billing, let me know and I’ll get a short-term invoice prepared.

Thanks,
Hannah

[Attachments: RDW_temp_burst_SOW_draft.pdf, proposed_invoice_terms_v1.pdf]
[Links: DocuSign template will be shared when you confirm SOW path]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: quick clarifications on credit and accounting

Hannah / Ben — quick finance notes so we’re aligned before sending DocuSign: 

- We can approve a $3,500 one-time credit for marketing/launch gestures on deals < $250k ARR with AE sign-off; need your confirmation that this is a one-off and is not to be treated as an ongoing discount.
- Accounting will post the credit as a contra-revenue line on the next invoice; if Aurora requests an immediate cash refund instead of a credit memo that will require CFO approval and will delay the process.
- For the temporary reserved uplift option (if they choose 30-day reserved commit), we should collect a PO and issue a pro-forma invoice before provisioning.

If we want to include a clause that the credit is contingent on SOW being signed within 48 hours, I recommend clear language in the DocuSign template.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Emily Zhao <emily@aurora-health.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate increase for product launch

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our procurement constraints. We’ll sign the SOW and take the one-time credit offer.

A few quick confirmations:
- Please set the burst window to UTC 2026-02-19 00:00 — 2026-02-22 00:00.
- We’ll route DocuSign to procurement; email for PO: procurement@aurora-health.com.
- Can you confirm whether the credit applies if actual peak usage ends up <30M/day? (We expect peaks but want to ensure we still get the credit if uplift is unused.)

Please send the DocuSign link and the final SOW with the 48-hour signature clause and we’ll process on our side.

Best,
Emily

---
Emily Zhao
Director of Product, Aurora Health

Emily — perfect. We’ll:

1) Send DocuSign (template: https://app.docusign.com/templates/ABC-TempBurst-2026) with the 48-hour signature clause per Laura’s guidance.
2) Provision the temporary uplift to start at 2026-02-19 00:00 UTC; Ben will coordinate the ramp.
3) Apply the $3,500 one-time credit to your next invoice regardless of peak utilization (credit is conditional on SOW signature within 48 hours).

Procurement note: please send PO to procurement@redwood.ai if you choose a reserved uplift path; otherwise DocuSign is fine for the SOW route.

Sending DocuSign now. Thanks and good luck on launch — we’ll monitor closely over the window.

—Hannah
